disposition_reason: Mini review of selenium uptake, assimilation and biofortification effects on crop secondary metabolites.
non_numeric_findings: Selenium deficiency is thought to affect 800 million people worldwide, per the review (p. 1).
Plants take up selenate through sulfate transporters (p. 1).
Seleniferous sites contain more than 1 and up to 100 mg/kg soil selenium; plant selenium at such sites may vary over 100-fold between species (p. 2).
Some organic forms such as methylselenocysteine appear to be particularly effective dietary sources (p. 1).
Selenium fertilization can change sulfur- and nitrogen-containing secondary metabolites such as glucosinolates in broccoli (p. 3).
